title: Philly Cheesesteaks with Shaved Ribeye and Soft Onions
summary: Partly frozen ribeye is shaved paper-thin, seared hard in batches, drained, combined with golden onions, topped with melting white cheese and scooped into toasted rolls.
equipment: large heavy frying pan or flat griddle (cast iron ideal)

steps.title: Freeze the steak
steps.text: Put the steak on a tray in the freezer for 45-60 minutes until very firm but not frozen solid.

steps.title: Toast the rolls
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Split the rolls lengthwise, leaving a hinge, and toast on a tray for 5 minutes until lightly crisp.

steps.title: Shave the beef
steps.text: Slice the firm steak as thinly as possible across the grain, then roughly chop the pile 10-15 times.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in the pan over medium heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden. Tip out.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil over high heat until smoking. Add the beef in one layer and cook undisturbed for 3 minutes until browned underneath, then stir for 1-2 minutes until no pink remains (at least 63 °C). Drain in the colander, then return to the pan over medium heat with the onions and pepper.

steps.title: Melt the cheese
steps.text: Divide the meat into 4 long piles, lay 2 slices of cheese over each and cover for 1 minute until melted.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Slide a spatula under each pile, scoop it into a roll and serve hot.

tips: Freezing the steak first is what makes the paper-thin slices possible.
Draining the meat stops the roll going soggy.
Mild provolone is the other classic cheese if you can't find white American.
storage: Best eaten hot. Refrigerate leftover filling within 1 hour, use within 3 days and reheat until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
